title: AI in GTM at Notion — Flora Liu
talk_summary: Notion's GTM engineering team replaced a fragmented tool spiderweb with a single decisioning system built on four layers (know/decide/act/learn), where agents operate as first-class operators on the same context substrate as humans. Key mechanisms: a rented durable workflow engine (Temporal) for retries/dedupes, a consolidated denormalized context layer, first-class eligibility/routing primitives, and full tracing of every LLM step.

takeaways.technique: Durable workflow engine for multi-step agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Each signal becomes a workflow on Temporal (rented), so retries, dedupes, and resume-from-failure are handled by the engine rather than hand-rolled; one malformed input can't take down a batch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: temporal lets us focus on writing the sequential logic for our GTM use cases while it will handle the retries, ddupes um and handling and going back to exactly where failures left off

takeaways.what_they_do: They publish a denormalized profile keyed by account/contact IDs in a KV store so agents query in milliseconds with no joins; agent-generated artifacts (research snippets, rolling summaries) are keyed by the same IDs so downstream reads everything in one shot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We publish a denormalized key addressable profile that agents can quickly query in milliseconds with no joins.

takeaways.what_they_do: For cold outbound, a research sub-agent runs concurrent research, drafts three emails, they are scored, and a review agent picks the highest-scoring one and edits it, looping until ready.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there should be three of them so they're scored and then a review agent will pick the highest scoring one and make any updates if necessary

takeaways.technique: Trace every LLM step and thread outcomes to decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: Every LLM step is traced for quality evaluation, and every action is a decision log with outcomes threaded back to the decision that caused it, feeding the decision layer so the system self-improves.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every LLM step is traced so that we can evaluate quality and improve over time.

takeaways.technique: Signal service emits concrete tasks to human or agent
takeaways.what_they_do: A signal service watches the customer profile, decides whether a single action is available and who should own it, then emits a concrete task that lands in a database for a human or agent to pick up.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it emits a concrete task following the architecture I described before. And this task could be for a human or an agent.

takeaways.technique: Treat external input as untrusted; humans approve agent actions by default
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately don't let agents talk directly to customers; humans approve agent output by default, and externally sourced input (contact-sales forms) is treated as untrusted so trust boundaries don't break down with an agent in the middle.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we treat that as untrusted user input. And so trust boundaries don't break down, especially because there is an agent in the middle.
